front: What are the four mandatory component files of a complete Esri Shapefile?
back: .shp (geometry), .shx (spatial index), .dbf (attribute database table), and .prj (projection coordinate definition).

front: What is On-The-Fly (OTF) Reprojection in QGIS?
back: The automatic mathematical conversion of layers stored in different CRSs into the project's display CRS in real time without altering source files.

front: What units are used by Geographic Coordinate Systems such as WGS 84 (EPSG:4326)?
back: Angular units (decimal degrees of latitude and longitude).

front: What units are used by Projected Coordinate Systems such as UTM Zone 13N (EPSG:26913)?
back: Linear metric units (meters of Easting and Northing).

front: Why is Web Mercator (EPSG:3857) widely used for web mapping despite area distortion?
back: It is conformal, meaning it preserves local right angles and street shapes perfectly, allowing rapid square tile generation and intuitive local navigation.

front: What is the 'Greenland Problem' in cartography?
back: The massive visual exaggeration of high-latitude landmasses on cylindrical conformal maps (like Mercator), making Greenland appear the size of Africa when it is actually 1/14th its size.

front: What is the difference between planimetric and ellipsoidal distance measurements?
back: Planimetric measures across a flat 2D map ignoring curvature; ellipsoidal measures the true shortest geodesic distance across Earth's 3D curved surface.

What is the difference between precision and accuracy in GIS measurements?
back: Precision is the degree of detail or decimal places reported; accuracy is how close the measurement is to the true real-world value.

front: What is the core takeaway of GEOG 1115L Lab 2 regarding coordinates?
back: A coordinate is not an inherent fact about a place; it is a measurement taken relative to a chosen reference frame and datum.
